title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Summary:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standardized on-call and incident response process. It covers the incident lifecycle, role definitions, on-call rotations, escalation policies, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates. The goal is to resolve incidents quickly, minimize customer impact, and capture learnings to prevent recurrence.

1) Incident lifecycle (detect → resolve → learn)

  - Detection: Alerts surface via PagerDuty, CloudWatch/Prometheus, logging anomaly detectors, or customer reports.
  - Triage: On-call primary evaluates scope, severity, and impact. If unclear, escalate to secondary and follow the escalation policy below.
  - Mobilize: Assign Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).
  - Mitigation & Recovery: Apply runbook steps to restore service or enact mitigations (rate limiting, fallback models, traffic shifting).
  - Post-incident: Capture timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items in a postmortem. Track action ownership and due dates.

2) Severity definitions and thresholds

  - Sev 0 (SEV0) — Production outage: System unavailable for >5% of customers or >5 minutes for critical API. PagerDuty: immediate escalation. SLO impact: <99.5% availability.
  - Sev 1 (SEV1) — High impact: Significant degradation (e.g., model serving >500ms p95 increase affecting >20% traffic). PagerDuty: page on-call primary.
  - Sev 2 (SEV2) — Partial degradation: Reduced performance or partial feature loss. Notification via on-call channel.
  - Sev 3 (SEV3) — Non-urgent: Low-impact bugs, single-customer issues, scheduled maintenance items.

Alert thresholds (examples):
  - API 5xx rate >1% for 10 minutes → Sev1
  - p95 latency increase >2x baseline for 5 minutes and request volume >100 reqs/min → Sev1
  - GPU OOM on serving node (repeated) → Sev1
  - Ingestion lag >30 minutes for embeddings pipeline → Sev2

3) Roles & responsibilities

  - On-call Primary (Primary): First responder. Responsible for initial triage, mitigation steps, paging secondary if needed, and documenting timeline.
  - On-call Secondary (Secondary): Backup for primary. Handles escalations, takes over if primary unavailable.
  - Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team effort for Sev1/SEV0 incidents, drives decision-making and runbook execution. Typically assigned by the on-call rotation lead or SRE.
  - Communications Lead: Owns internal Slack status channel, status page updates, and customer comms drafts.
  - Postmortem Owner: Writes the postmortem, ensures findings and action items are tracked and closed. Usually the IC or service owner.
  - SMEs: Domain experts (runtime, infra, model-serving, infra-network) pulled in as needed.

4) Escalation policy

  1. PagerDuty page to primary. Wait 2 minutes for acknowledgement.
  2. If no ack, escalate to secondary. Wait 3 minutes.
  3. If still unacknowledged or issue is SEV0, page SRE lead and engage IC immediately.
  4. For customer-impacting incidents, Communications Lead drafts status page message within 10 minutes.

PagerDuty example policy (summary):
  - Level 1: On-call primary (rotate weekly)
  - Level 2: On-call secondary (rotate weekly)
  - Level 3: SRE lead / Eng manager (on-call rotation for major weekends)

5) On-call rotations and handoff

  - Rotation cadence: Primary rotates weekly (Mon 09:00 PT → next Mon 09:00 PT). Secondary rotates on the same cadence but offset by team preference.
  - Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack #oncall-handoff channel):
    1. Confirm you are scheduled and reachable.
    2. Review open incidents and ongoing mitigations.
    3. Confirm runbook links and playbooks for services you own.
    4. Note planned releases or maintenance windows during your shift.
  - Escalation contact list (example):
    - SRE PagerDuty group: pd-sre@redwood.com
    - Runtime team lead: runtime-leads@redwood.com
    - Platform on-call Slack: #oncall-runtime

6) Runbook template and examples

Runbook structure (one page per incident type / service):
  - Title: Short descriptive name (e.g., "Model-serving high p95 latency")
  - Symptoms: Alerts and customer reports that indicate this incident
  - Impact: What is affected (APIs, customers, regions)
  - Severity mapping: Which severity to assign based on impact thresholds
  - Quick mitigation steps (ordered): immediate actions to reduce customer impact
  - Diagnostic commands / queries: concrete commands and Prometheus/Grafana queries
  - Root cause hints: Known causes and checks to verify them
  - Rollback / recovery steps: Commands to restore service or rollback releases
  - Contacts / escalation path: owners and emails/pager contacts
  - Post-incident checklist: data collection, timeline, postmortem owner assignment

Example runbook snippet (Model-serving high p95 latency):
  - Symptoms:
    - p95 latency spike observed in grafana: service: model-serving p95 > 800ms for 10m
    - Increase in queue length on inference-workers metric: inference_queue_length > 50
  - Quick mitigations:
    1. Identify recent model rollouts: curl -s "https://internal-api/models/active" | jq .
    2. Temporarily shift traffic to previous model variant: /scripts/traffic-shift --service model-serving --to stable
    3. Scale up replica count: kubectl scale deploy model-serving --replicas=10 -n production
    4. If repeated GPU OOMs, set NODE_SELECTOR to isolate affected nodes and drain them.
  - Diagnostic queries:
    - Prometheus: rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{job="model-serving"}[5m])
    - Grafana dashboard: Model Serving → p95 latency by model

7) Common incident table (quick reference)

Incident type | Symptoms | First-action (5 min) | Escalate if
---------------|----------|----------------------|-------------
Control plane outage | API 503 across regions | Verify control plane health, failover to standby control plane | >5 min or >5% customers impacted
Model-serving high latency | p95 >2x baseline | Shift traffic to stable variant, scale replicas | latency persists after mitigations
GPU OOMs / node crashes | Repeated OOMs on node | Drain node, cordon, rotate model to other nodes | OOMs across >1 node
Embedding ingestion lag | Ingestion backlog >30m | Restart consumer, increase parallelism | backlog continues >60m

8) Postmortem requirements

  - Applicability: All SEV0 and SEV1 incidents require a postmortem within 72 hours of incident resolution. SEV2 incidents may require a postmortem if customer impact occurred.
  - Postmortem template (must include):
    - Title and incident ID
    - Summary (one-paragraph customer-facing description)
    - Timeline (UTC timestamps)
    - Root cause analysis (with evidence)
    - Contributing factors
    - Immediate mitigations and long-term fixes
    - Action items (owner, due date, status)
    - Detection & response metrics (MTTA, MTTR)
    - Lessons learned and follow-ups
  - Review: Postmortem reviewed in weekly SRE retro and action items tracked until closed.

9) Game days and readiness exercises

  - Frequency: Quarterly team-level game days; annual company-wide resilience week.
  - Scope: Simulated network partitions, model-serving degradation, control plane failover, and data corruption scenarios.
  - Objectives: Validate runbooks, verify escalation paths, improve cross-team coordination, and measure MTTR improvements.
  - After-action: Each game day must produce a short report with observations, action items, and schedule for follow-up fixes.

10) Status page & customer communication templates

Status page guidance:
  - Update cadence: initial update within 10 minutes for SEV0/SEV1, follow-ups every 30-60 minutes while incident is active, and a final update when resolved.
  - Content requirements: Impact statement, affected regions/services, user-visible symptoms, mitigation in progress, ETA when possible, and link to postmortem when available.

Customer-facing status template (initial):
  - Title: "Service disruption: [service-name] - [short impact]"
  - Body: "We are investigating reports of [symptoms]. Some customers in [regions] may experience [impact]. Our on-call team has been engaged and is investigating. We will provide an update by [time] or sooner."

Customer-facing status template (update):
  - Title: "Update: [service-name] - [current brief status]"
  - Body: "Our team has identified [root-cause or suspected cause] and is applying [mitigation]. The current scope is [users/regions]. We estimate restoration in approximately [ETA]. We will post another update at [time]."

Post-resolution message:
  - Title: "Resolved: [service-name] - [short reason]"
  - Body: "Service has been restored. Root cause analysis is ongoing and we will publish a full postmortem within 72 hours if this incident met SEV0/SEV1 criteria. Sorry for the disruption and thank you for your patience."

11) Tools, dashboards and links (examples)

  - PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com (on-call schedules & escalation policies)
  - Statuspage: https://status.redwood.ai (public status page)
  - Grafana dashboards: /grafana/d/model-serving, /grafana/d/control-plane-health
  - Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks-index
  - Incident tracking: Jira project RED-INCIDENTS (label: incident)

12) Metrics and SLOs to track for incident response

  - Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA) — target <2 minutes for SEV0/SEV1 alerts
  - Mean Time To Mitigate (MTTM) — target <15 minutes for SEV1
  - Mean Time To Recover (MTTR) — target <60 minutes for SEV1
  - Post-incident action closure rate — target 100% of SEV0 action items closed within 90 days

13) Ownership and governance

  - On-call policy owner: Eng-SRE (contact: eng-sre@redwood.com)
  - Playbook maintenance: Service owners must keep service-specific runbooks up to date; SRE will audit runbooks quarterly.
  - Exceptions: Any deviation from this process (e.g., different rotation cadence for a special project) must be documented and approved by Eng-SRE and the relevant service owner.

Appendices:
  - A: Slack templates (incident start)
    - "[INCIDENT] SEV1: {service} - {short description}. IC: @user. Join #incident-{id} for coordination."
  - B: Slack templates (status page post)
    - "Status update: {link to status} - {brief summary} - next update in 30m."
  - C: Quick diagnostic commands (k8s & logs)
    - kubectl -n production get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide
    - kubectl logs -n production deployment/model-serving --since=10m | tail -n 200
    - aws s3 ls s3://redwood-embeddings-backups/ --human-readable --summarize | tail -n 50

Questions or updates to this playbook should be sent to the Eng-SRE team and proposed as edits on this page.
